title: Halloween
tagline: Laurie's been prepping for forty years. Dinner takes two hours.
about: Forty years after she survived one Halloween night, Laurie Strode has spent her life preparing for the masked man's return, and on the eve of his transfer, he gets out.
cue: Serve the jerky when Aaron holds up Michael's mask at Smith's Grove.

    Before the DanceThe Main EventLast Dance SweetsThe Punch Bowl
    Before the DanceBabysitter's pizza scrollsPizza dough scrolls with tomato, mozzarella, oregano and parmesan, with warm garlic tomato dipHow to make it500g pizza dough100g tomato passata, for the filling1 tsp dried oregano200g mozzarella, grated40g parmesan, grated1 tbsp olive oil300g tomato passata, for the dip1 garlic clove, crushed1/2 tsp chilli flakes1/2 tsp saltHeat the oven to 200°C, line a tray and roll the dough into a 40 x 30cm rectangle.Spread with the passata for the filling and sprinkle with the oregano, mozzarella and half the parmesan.Roll up from the long side, cut into 12 scrolls and lay them cut side up. Brush with the oil and sprinkle with the rest of the parmesan.Rest the scrolls so they puff.Bake until golden.Simmer the passata for the dip with the garlic, chilli flakes and salt and serve warm with the scrolls.Laurie's stockpile beef jerkyThin beef strips marinated in soy, brown sugar, garlic and smoked paprika, dried low until chewyHow to make it750g beef topside, trimmed125ml soy sauce2 tbsp brown sugar2 tbsp Worcestershire sauce1 tsp smoked paprika1 tsp garlic powder1 tsp onion powder1 tsp black pepper, cracked1/2 tsp chilli flakesFreeze the beef to firm it up for slicing.Slice the beef 4mm thick against the grain.Whisk the soy, sugar, Worcestershire and spices, toss the beef through and marinate in the fridge.Heat the oven to 75°C, pat the strips dry and lay them on wire racks over trays.Dry in the oven with the door slightly open, turning once, until leathery but still bendy.Cool before packing.Spinach and artichoke dipVicky's babysitting snack, before the closet door opens.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.The Main EventLaurie's safe room chilliSlow-simmered beef chuck chilli with chipotle, black beans and tomato, with sour cream, cheddar and corn chipsHow to make it1kg beef chuck, in 3cm cubes1 tsp salt2 tbsp vegetable oil2 onions, diced1 red capsicum, diced4 garlic cloves, crushed2 chipotle chillies in adobo, chopped2 tsp ground cumin2 tsp smoked paprika1 tsp dried oregano2 tbsp tomato paste400g tin crushed tomatoes500ml beef stock800g tinned black beans, drained20g dark chocolate150g sour cream100g cheddar, grated200g corn chips1 lime, in wedgesSeason the beef with the salt and brown in batches in the oil.Soften the onions and capsicum in the pot.Stir in the garlic, chipotle, cumin, paprika, oregano and tomato paste.Add the tomatoes and stock, return the beef, cover and simmer until tender.Stir in the beans and chocolate and simmer uncovered to thicken.Serve with sour cream, cheddar, corn chips and lime wedges.Strode family dinner roast chicken and pumpkinWhole bird with lemon and thyme, roasted with red onion and potatoes, gravy, Karen's normal nightHow to make it1.8kg whole chicken1 lemon4 sprigs of thyme600g pumpkin, in wedges600g potatoes, in chunks2 red onions, in wedges3 tbsp olive oil300ml chicken stock1 tbsp plain flour100g mixed salad leavesHeat the oven to 200°C. Stuff the chicken with the halved lemon and thyme, rub with oil and salt.Roast the chicken with the vegetables tossed in oil until golden and cooked through.Rest the chicken. Stir the flour and stock into the tray juices and simmer for gravy.Carve and serve with the vegetables, gravy and salad.Last Dance SweetsBurning basement whoopie piesChocolate rounds, orange buttercream. Laurie lights the trapHow to make it250g plain flour40g cocoa powder1 tsp bicarb soda1/4 tsp salt115g butter, softened, for the cakes200g brown sugar1 egg2 tsp vanilla extract250ml buttermilk125g butter, softened, for the filling250g icing sugar1 tbsp milk1/4 tsp orange food colouringHeat the oven to 180°C and line two trays.Whisk the flour, cocoa, bicarb and salt.Beat the butter for the cakes with the sugar until pale, then beat in the egg and half the vanilla.Fold in the dry mix and buttermilk alternately.Spoon 24 rounds onto the trays and bake until springy.Cool the cakes.Beat the butter for the filling with the icing sugar, milk, the rest of the vanilla and the colouring until fluffy.Sandwich the cakes together in pairs.The Punch BowlLaurie's rye and gingerRye, ginger beer and lime.
